title: Method Overloading in a Calculator
objective: Declare overloaded instance methods that differ by parameter count and type.
description:
Create a class Calculator with these overloaded methods:
- add(int a, int b) returns the sum of two integers.
- add(int a, int b, int c) returns the sum of three integers.
- add(double a, double b) returns the sum of two decimal numbers.
Read the seven input values in the specified order. Call the matching overload for each group and print each result on a separate line. Format the decimal result to two places using Locale.US.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: Java selects the correct overload based on the number and types of arguments.
input_format:
Lines 1–2: two integers.
Lines 3–5: three integers.
Lines 6–7: two decimal numbers.
output_format: Print the first sum, second sum, and decimal sum on separate lines.

hint_2: Read the last two values as doubles so the add(double, double) version is chosen.
hint_3: Only the decimal result is formatted with two places.
